doc: Payload budgets per consumer profile (kemiller2002/limen#19). Each budget is the measured baseline plus 10%, rounded up to a whole KiB; test/bench-size.test.ts fails when a profile exceeds its budget or loads a forbidden module. Raising a budget needs its own work item saying what grew and why; lowering one after an optimization is encouraged.

history.change: Initial baselines and budgets (kemiller2002/limen#19).

Re-baselined every profile after the binding security policy (src/kernel/binding-policy.ts, kemiller2002/limen#18): each profile that loads the kernel grew by about 2.1 KB gzip (6.8 KB raw). kernel-only and kernel-with-handles exceeded their budgets; the rest had not, but are re-baselined by the same rule so every budget keeps 10% headroom over what ships.
Added kernel-with-focus (kemiller2002/limen#23): the focus pack adds 3876 bytes gzip over kernel-only, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-schedule (kemiller2002/limen#24): the scheduling pack adds 2689 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-measure (kemiller2002/limen#25): the measurement pack adds 5605 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.
Added kernel-with-events (kemiller2002/limen#29): the events pack adds 6208 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it.

Added kernel-with-overlay (kemiller2002/limen#49): the overlay pack, with the shared named-target resolver, adds 5614 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/overlay/.

Added kernel-with-realtime (kemiller2002/limen#26): the realtime pack, with the shared handle table, adds 5841 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/realtime/.

Added kernel-with-files (kemiller2002/limen#27): the files pack, with the shared handle table and target resolver, adds 6348 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/files/.

Added kernel-with-store (kemiller2002/limen#28): the IndexedDB store pack adds 9456 bytes gzip over the kernel (its generated codec is the largest part: the transaction and schema contract is the widest yet), and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/store/.

Added kernel-with-adapters (kemiller2002/limen#30): the adapter host pack, with the shared handle table and target resolver, adds 7419 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it; the reference Web Component adapter is a separate module and is not in this profile. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/adapters/.

Re-baselined every profile after the Core HTTP profile, protocol 1.3 (kemiller2002/limen#47): Core's generated codec gained the new request and outcome types, and the kernel's Http path gained the response representations, header selection and the XSRF binding. Measured on kernel-with-overlay before and after: +1729 bytes gzip (+6640 raw), on every profile that loads the kernel. kernel-only, minimal-consumer, kernel-with-handles, the two host profiles and kernel-with-focus exceeded their budgets; the rest are re-baselined by the same rule so every budget keeps 10% headroom over what ships. The remaining growth since WI-0053 on the older profiles (about 0.9 KB gzip on kernel-only) is protocol 1.2 form-control state, IME handling and boolean attributes, which had stayed within budget.

Added kernel-with-transfer (kemiller2002/limen#47): the transfer profile pack adds 5340 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. The files pack gained its explicit fileFor accessor (+157 raw bytes, within its budget). Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/transfer/.
Added kernel-with-fallback-host (kemiller2002/limen#50): the optional fatal-fallback host adds 2340 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that use it.

Added kernel-with-presentation (kemiller2002/limen#34): the resource-hint and view-transition pack adds 4060 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/presentation/.

Added kernel-with-environment (kemiller2002/limen#35): the environment evidence and formatting pack adds 4979 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* capability profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/environment/.

Added kernel-with-lifecycle (kemiller2002/limen#43): the page, connectivity and lifecycle evidence pack adds 5735 bytes gzip over the kernel, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* capability profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/lifecycle/.

Re-baselined minimal-consumer after protocol 1.4 (kemiller2002/limen#40): OutcomeUnknownReason in the generated Core codec and the kernel classifying a thrown fetch by method and connectivity. Measured on minimal-consumer against the commit before WI-0103: +497 bytes gzip (+1686 raw), which put it 80 bytes over its budget. Most of its growth since WI-0085 (29279 against a 26764 baseline, +2515 bytes gzip) came earlier and stayed within headroom: chiefly WI-0089 projection atomicity, WI-0090 kernel status and dispose, and WI-0092 lazy federation in the package root. Only that profile is re-baselined; every other profile stays within its existing budget and keeps its baseline.

Added kernel-with-offline (kemiller2002/limen#40): the service-worker registration and update pack adds 4451 bytes gzip over the kernel (measured against kernel-only as it ships now), and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* capability profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/offline/.

Added kernel-with-worker-host (kemiller2002/limen#41): the page side of the worker host adds 2136 bytes gzip over the kernel as it ships now; the engine and the worker-side module load in the worker, never the page.

Added kernel-with-geolocation and kernel-with-credentials (kemiller2002/limen#42): the two permission-sensitive packs add 5128 and 6842 bytes gzip over the kernel as it ships now, including the shared capability-support/permissions module, and only to applications that register them. Earlier kernel-with-* capability profiles now also forbid both.

Added kernel-with-coordination (kemiller2002/limen#46): the cross-context coordination pack adds 6841 bytes gzip over the kernel as it ships now, and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* capability profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/coordination/.

Re-baselined kernel-with-handles after WI-0116 (kemiller2002/limen#38): binding <head> and allowing the inert page-metadata forms add about 450 bytes gzip to every profile that loads the kernel, which put this profile 9 bytes over. Also corrected the baselines recorded for minimal-consumer (WI-0105) and the profiles added in WI-0100, WI-0106, WI-0108, WI-0110 and WI-0114: they were measured with a relative root, which orders the bundled modules differently from test/bench-size.test.ts and changes the bundled gzip size by a few hundred bytes (raw bytes are identical). They are now measured exactly as the test measures them, and their budgets follow from the same 10% rule; the new baselines also include the kernel growth since each was recorded (protocol 1.4, WI-0103, where it came after them, and WI-0116), so none of the differences is the capability packs themselves growing.

Lowered minimal-consumer (kemiller2002/limen#61): the package root no longer exports federation or the reference engine, so the minimal consumer loads Core only. Measured with an absolute root: 144579 -> 114362 raw bytes, 30286 -> 23819 gzip bundled. It now also forbids dist/federation.js, dist/engine/ and dist/renderer/.

Added renderer (kemiller2002/limen#38): the optional server and static renderer, 87066 raw / 16648 gzip bytes bundled, measured with an absolute root. It runs on a server or at build time, never in a page; its closure must hold no BrowserKernel, pack, federation, reference engine, host or tooling.

Added kernel-with-media (kemiller2002/limen#44): the capture and recording pack, with the shared permission, handle and target support, adds 11837 bytes gzip over the kernel (measured with an absolute root), and only to applications that register it. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/media/.

Added kernel-with-peer (kemiller2002/limen#44): the WebRTC peer connection pack adds 7867 bytes gzip over the kernel (absolute root), and only to applications that register it; it never loads the media pack or the permission support. Earlier kernel-with-* profiles now also forbid dist/capabilities/peer/. kernel-with-media grew 31 bytes gzip with the streamFor accessor, within its budget.

Re-baselined kernel-only after WI-0043 (projection compares with the live DOM before writing): +80 bytes gzip (22504 -> 22584), which put it 56 bytes over a budget last set in WI-0085. Most of the headroom had gone to growth that stayed within budget since then (protocol 1.4, the head-binding policy of WI-0116). Measured with an absolute root.

Re-baselined every profile that loads the kernel (absolute root). kernel-with-files had gone 31 bytes over after WI-0043 (compare-before-write) and WI-0044 (remove before reorder); its baseline, like most, predated in-budget kernel growth since WI-0085: protocol 1.4 (WI-0103), head binding and the metadata policy (WI-0116), and those two. Every budget again keeps 10% headroom over what ships. Gzip bundled, old baseline -> new: kernel-only 22584->22677; kernel-with-handles 23561->23729; kernel-with-dotnet-host 20967->23459; kernel-with-raw-host 21780->24278; kernel-with-worker-host 24619->24792; kernel-with-focus 24028->26553; kernel-with-schedule 22850->25375; kernel-with-measure 25765->28320; kernel-with-events 26679->29198; kernel-with-overlay 25769->28324; kernel-with-realtime 25994->28545; kernel-with-files 26528->29727; kernel-with-store 29607->32118; kernel-with-adapters 27612->30132; kernel-with-transfer 25489->28047; kernel-with-fallback-host 23831->25021; kernel-with-presentation 25551->26763; kernel-with-environment 26470->27693; kernel-with-lifecycle 26916->27099; kernel-with-offline 26831->27013; kernel-with-geolocation 27434->27601; kernel-with-credentials 29804->29966; kernel-with-coordination 29992->30152; kernel-with-media 34341->34535; kernel-with-peer 30371->30533.

profiles.name: minimal-consumer
profiles.doc: What examples/minimal (the copy shipped in the package, and the minimal root consumer of kemiller2002/limen#61) loads: the package root, which is Limen Core only. Federation, the reference engine and every optional layer are forbidden here.

profiles.name: kernel-only
profiles.doc: The ./kernel subpath: BrowserKernel and what it needs, nothing else.

profiles.name: kernel-with-handles
profiles.doc: A representative optional set: the kernel plus capability-support's handle table, the library every handle-returning pack imports.

profiles.name: kernel-with-dotnet-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the .NET WebAssembly host adapter (F# and C# guests), excluding the .NET runtime itself.

profiles.name: kernel-with-raw-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the raw WebAssembly host adapter (Rust guest), excluding the .wasm module.

profiles.name: kernel-with-worker-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the worker host adapter's page side (./hosts/worker), as a page whose engine runs in a dedicated worker loads them. The worker's own modules and the engine load in the worker, not the page.

profiles.name: kernel-with-focus
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the focus, selection and scroll capability pack (./capabilities/focus), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-schedule
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the scheduling capability pack (./capabilities/schedule), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-measure
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the measurement and observer capability pack (./capabilities/measure), with the capability-support libraries it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-events
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the rich browser event facts capability pack (./capabilities/events), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-overlay
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the overlay and top-layer capability pack (./capabilities/overlay), with the capability-support target resolver it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-realtime
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the realtime and streaming capability pack (./capabilities/realtime), with the capability-support handle table it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-files
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the user-mediated file capability pack (./capabilities/files), with the capability-support libraries it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-store
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the IndexedDB structured-storage capability pack (./capabilities/store), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-adapters
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the governed adapter host pack (./capabilities/adapters), with the capability-support libraries it imports, as an application that registers it loads them. Adapters themselves, including the reference Web Component adapter, load separately.

profiles.name: kernel-with-transfer
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the HTTP transfer profile pack (./capabilities/transfer), as an application that registers it loads them. Uploading picked files also loads the files pack, which has its own profile.

profiles.name: kernel-with-fallback-host
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the optional fatal-fallback host (./hosts/fallback), as a composition root that uses it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-presentation
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the resource-hint and view-transition capability pack (./capabilities/presentation), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-environment
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the environment evidence and formatting capability pack (./capabilities/environment), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-lifecycle
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the page, connectivity and lifecycle evidence capability pack (./capabilities/lifecycle), as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-offline
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the service-worker registration and update capability pack (./capabilities/offline), as an application that registers it loads them. The worker module itself runs in the service worker, not the page.

profiles.name: kernel-with-geolocation
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the device-location pack under the permission pattern (./capabilities/geolocation) and the shared permission support it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-credentials
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the WebAuthn passkey pack under the permission pattern (./capabilities/credentials) and the shared permission support it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-coordination
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the cross-context coordination pack (./capabilities/coordination), as an application that registers it loads them. The hub module runs in the SharedWorker, not the page.

profiles.name: renderer
profiles.doc: The optional server and static renderer (./renderer, kemiller2002/limen#38): what a server or build step loads to render a route. It reuses the kernel's pure binding policy and handshake, never the BrowserKernel itself.

profiles.name: kernel-with-media
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the camera and microphone capture and recording pack (./capabilities/media) and the shared permission, handle and target support it imports, as an application that registers it loads them.

profiles.name: kernel-with-peer
profiles.doc: The kernel plus the WebRTC peer connection pack (./capabilities/peer) and the shared handle and target support it imports, as an application that registers it loads them. It does not load the media pack: an application that sends a camera registers both and hands the peer pack the media pack's captures.
